record.original_question: If a and b are distinct positive nonintegers, then for every ergodic system (X, X, µ, T) and bounded functions f, g, must the averages (1/N) Σ f(T^[n^a] x) g(T^[n^b] x) converge almost everywhere to ∫f dµ · ∫g dµ?

evidence.quote: Problem 24. Let a, b be distinct positive non-integers. Show that for every ergodic system (X, X , µ, T) and functions f, g ∈ L∞(µ), we have lim 1/N Σ f(T^[n^a]x) · g(T^[n^b]x) = ∫ f dµ · ∫ g dµ for almost every x ∈ X.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $a$ and $b$ be distinct positive non-integers. Let $(X,\mathcal{X},\mu,T)$ be an ergodic measure-preserving system, where $T:X\to X$ is an invertible measurable transformation preserving the probability measure $\mu$, and ergodicity means every $T$-invariant measurable set has measure $0$ or $1$. For real $t$, let $[t]$ denote the integer part of $t$. Determine whether, for every such system and every pair of bounded measurable functions $f,g\in L^\infty(\mu)$, the averages
$$\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N} f(T^{[n^a]}x)\, g(T^{[n^b]}x)$$
converge, as $N\to\infty$, to $\left(\int f\,d\mu\right)\left(\int g\,d\mu\right)$ for $\mu$-almost every $x\in X$.
artifact.category_tag: pointwise multiple ergodic averages along Hardy sequences
artifact.status_search_result: The deterministic pointwise convergence problem for bilinear ergodic averages along fractional power sequences $[n^a],[n^b]$ is listed among Frantzikinakis' open problems. Although random and polynomial bilinear analogues (e.g., Krause–Mirek–Tao for $n,n^2$) and related joint ergodicity results have been established, the deterministic Hardy-power case with distinct positive non-integers $a,b$ remains open as of recent surveys and 2024–2025 work.

status_evidence.claim: The problem is explicitly stated as an open problem in Frantzikinakis' open problems list.

status_evidence.title: Pointwise ergodic theorems for non-conventional bilinear polynomial averages
status_evidence.snippet: Pointwise convergence for bilinear polynomial ergodic averages.
status_evidence.claim: Polynomial bilinear analogues are settled, but Hardy-power deterministic case is not covered.

status_evidence.title: Random sequences and pointwise convergence of multiple ergodic averages
status_evidence.snippet: Pointwise convergence for randomized [n^c]-type sequences; deterministic versions remain open.
status_evidence.claim: Indicates the deterministic [n^a],[n^b] bilinear case remains open.
